issues.description: The problem statement's UML and the solution expect a Stock method named addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) to add a new StockIngredient to the stock, but the template Stock class provides a method named addItem(StockIngredient) instead. This name/signature mismatch is a structural inconsistency: students following the UML or the solution may try to call addToStockIngredients and find it missing in the provided template, causing confusion or compilation errors.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the template Stock API match the UML and the solution. Either rename the template method addItem(StockIngredient) to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient), or add a new public method addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) that delegates to the existing addItem implementation. Alternatively, update the problem statement/UML to reference addItem instead of addToStockIngredients — but aligning the template to the UML/solution (adding addToStockIngredients) is the least disruptive change for students.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution repository use the Stock API method name addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient), but the template repository provides this functionality under the different name addItem(StockIngredient). This naming divergence for the same conceptual operation (adding a StockIngredient to the stock container) can confuse students: they will expect addToStockIngredients as shown in the UML/problem text and in the reference solution, but the starter code uses addItem, causing an unclear mapping and possible compile errors or wasted time searching for the method.
issues.suggested_fix: Align the template Stock API with the problem statement and solution by renaming the template method addItem(StockIngredient) to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient). Alternatively, add an addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) wrapper that delegates to addItem to preserve backward compatibility; ensure documentation/UML and starter code use the same name.
